capabilities_done: Binary reel-native-av1-worker (required-features av1; src/bin + src/worker.rs worker_main): hosts hsk_studio_reel::av1::Av1Decoder on a 32 MiB-stack thread; a stdin reader thread exits the process when the host closes stdin (parent gone mid-decode); a panic hook exits with code 70 so a rav1d abort ends the process at once without Windows Error Reporting

WorkerAv1Provider (src/host.rs): implements reel MediaProvider with id av1 (descriptor = reel av1::descriptor()); indexes and demuxes ISOBMFF/Matroska through reel's own providers in OutputMode::Packets (frame-accurate start, pre-roll), validates av1C with reel parse_av1c before any spawn, sends OPEN(config,color,bounds) + one PACKET per temporal unit + FINISH, forwards pictures to the caller's sink with the same tag matching, pre-roll drop, format-change refusal and receipt fields as reel's in-process Pump; decode_av1 returns Av1Error::{Reel, Worker(Av1WorkerFault)}, the MediaProvider port maps faults into ReelError

Wire protocol (src/wire.rs): hand-written u32-length-prefixed frames, kind+version+request-id header, caps checked before allocation, HELLO with protocol version + decoder id/version (host refuses a worker whose version differs: worker_version_mismatch), exact plane-length validation of every FRAME against its declared format, error classes as indices into a fixed static table (no string leaks), no new dependency

Supervision: per-request batch_deadline (default 30 s) and per-segment segment_deadline (default 300 s) on the real monotonic clock -> worker killed, decoder_deadline; cancel kills the worker (Canceled); reply cap = declared track dimensions x av1C chroma/bit depth (<= Limits::max_chunk_bytes) and decoder pixel limit = declared pixels (rav1d frame_size_limit) -> decoder_output_too_large; end of stream -> decoder_crashed{exit_code} with the process reaped; bounded respawn (max_spawns per spawn_window, default 16 per 10 s -> worker_respawn_limited); max_workers (default 2) alive at once -> worker_pool_busy; only Child handles this provider spawned are killed

Quiet spawn: CREATE_NO_WINDOW on Windows, env_clear (empty worker environment), stderr null, stdin/stdout piped; Av1WorkerStats (spawned, requests, crashed, killed_*, alive, last_crash_exit_code) makes every process action observable

Test fault injection in the worker (WorkerTestFault via env HSK_REEL_NATIVE_AV1_WORKER_TEST_FAULT, set only by Av1WorkerOptions): hang_on_packet, exit_on_packet, exit_on_open, oversize_frame, garbage_reply

Deterministic output: for mp4 and mkv, whole clip, random access with pre-roll and a two-frame span, the worker's chunk stream (pts, duration, index, flags, bytes) AND the whole SegmentReceipt (including bytes_read, decoder id/version, video format) are equal to reel's in-process decode; frame digests equal the libdav1d oracle SHA-256 in reel provenance.json

findings.text: A rav1d panic runs the Rust panic hook BEFORE the abort. The worker's hook calls process::exit(70), so the host sees end-of-stream and a prompt exit code instead of a process held alive ~5 s by Windows Error Reporting (motion-js finding wer-holds-aborted-worker). Needs no unsafe/SetErrorMode. Aborts that never reach the hook (stack overflow, foreign abort, allocation failure) are NOT converted: they are contained by the host kill at batch_deadline (decoder_deadline, or decoder_crashed with exit_code None).

Features are per package, so av1 on reel-native also links reel's in-process rav1d decoder into the host image (never called by this crate). The host still needs reel's av1 module only for descriptor(), DECODER_ID, decoder_version() and parse_av1c().

Cancel observed between packets returns Canceled without killing the worker (the session goes back to the pool; the next OPEN replaces any open decoder); cancel observed while a request is in flight kills the worker.

Frames larger than the container's declared track size (x av1C chroma/depth) are refused (decoder pixel limit + reply cap). Stricter than in-process reel, which only bounds by max_chunk_bytes. UNVERIFIED for AV1 streams whose render_size differs from the coded frame size and whose container declares the render size.

ReelError is closed, so contained faults cross the port as: decoder_crashed/worker_protocol -> Corrupt{what}, worker_version_mismatch -> Unsupported, decoder_deadline/decoder_output_too_large/worker_respawn_limited/worker_pool_busy -> LimitExceeded, worker_spawn_failed -> CodecUnavailable{av1}. UNVERIFIED mapping; the precise code is on Av1Error::code() through decode_av1.
Pictures already given to the sink before a fault stay delivered; an Err means the segment is incomplete (same as in-process Truncated semantics).

reel_api_requests.text: IsobmffProvider/MatroskaProvider::deliver route OutputMode::Decoded for av01/V_AV1 straight to crate::av1::decode_video_track when reel feature av1 is on; there is no hook to route decode to an external provider. Requested: an injectable video-decoder port (open(config,color,limits)/send(unit,tag)/finish/next_frame) on the providers or the Registry, so Registry::standard() consumers get the worker through the isobmff/matroska ids. WorkerAv1Provider currently re-implements reel's Pump matching (~60 lines) over OutputMode::Packets and is reached only through id av1.

Split reel feature av1 so the AV1 demux/config types (parse_av1c, Av1Config, descriptor, DECODER_ID) are available without the in-process rav1d decoder, or make the in-process path opt-in per call; today enabling reel-native/av1 forces the in-process decoder into the host image and leaves it reachable via the isobmff/matroska ids for untrusted input.
A ReelError variant (or code) for 'isolated decoder fault' (crash/deadline/protocol) would replace the UNVERIFIED mapping above.
pub verify_grant and check_cancel (or a Grant::verify) would remove two small duplicated helpers in host.rs.
